readsAs: a circle sliced into a grid of cells with one orange cell marked out
a hash or grid symbol inside a disc, like a window or a manhole cover
judge.why: The calm sliced-disc grid fits the brief, and the single orange cell nicely suggests a cohort being rolled out, but the cell only makes sense in color: in black or white it disappears into a plain hash-in-a-circle, and at 16–24px the thin gaps clog into a busy texture, so it stays a competent but forgettable grid mark.

readsAs: Clean grotesk wordmark whose t crossbar stretches over the a like a level platform or stage
A long horizontal stroke that can also read as a strikethrough
An 'St' monogram that looks like a font sample, not a mark
judge.why: The calm, precise sans and the stage-like crossbar fit platform teams, but the crossbar touches the top of the a and can look like a strikethrough, and the 'St' icon drops the long crossbar, so it ends up as a generic two-letter monogram whose rust brown fades on dark backgrounds and that won't hold up as a GitHub avatar or VS Code icon.

readsAs: a square spiral or Greek-key meander
a maze path that leads in to a centre square
a stylised lowercase 'b' or 'p' framed in a box
judge.why: The disciplined, monoline square path reaching a central square looks calm and precise and holds up from 16px to 256px in every colourway, but square spirals and meanders are a stock tech shape, and the idea of staged progress into a 'well' does not come through strongly enough to be ownable.
